newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares down on prospect of petrol price hike.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares down on prospect of petrol price hike.

text.p: Delhi shares slid further at mid-session as foreign institutional investors (FIIs) sold heavily on reports that the government might raise petroleum prices, brokers said.
At 1.00 p.m. (0730 GMT), the Delhi sensitive index was 23.23 points down at 645.91.

"Shares of ACC were also targets of FIIs and bear operators on account of the company's poor performance for the first half of the current financial year," said Rakesh Sharma of brokers Malhotra Financial Services.
But Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told Reuters Television in Tokyo that it would be difficult to raise the retail prices of petroleum products.
"Just last July we raised petroleum prices, it is difficult for the government to raise prices again," Chidamabaram said.
Leading cement maker ACC lost 142 rupees at 1,008 on poor first half results, 56 percent down compared to the same period a year ago.
Reliance Industries fell 5.25 rupees to 180. TISCO shed 3.70 rupees at 153.50. The country's largest banking firm State Bank of India dropped 3.20 rupees to 215.75.
Oriental Bank of Commerce quoted 1.55 rupees lower at 71.20. Larsen and Toubro fell 5.15 rupees to 210. ITC dropped three rupees to 270.
